fichas.title: Repair of damp foundations and building defects
fichas.summary: Most building defects are caused by damp. Rising damp may result from missing or defective damp-proofing, inadequate drainage, or defective rainwater goods. Repairs should investigate and remedy the source of moisture; where conventional waterproofing is impractical, special plaster systems can allow damp to evaporate, though they are less durable than plaster on a dry substrate.

fichas.summary: The details illustrate corner reinforcement with a metal angle, a sill-beam corner newly anchored with coach bolts, replacement of a sill beam in two stages, and possible corner joints for timber-frame sill beams under tension and compression. Additional connection details are labeled as jettied beam connections with dowels and cogged joints.

fichas.title: Waterproofing and drainage repairs to foundations and cellars
fichas.summary: The illustrated methods address water damage both without and under pressure. They include supplementary horizontal isolation and waterproofing of a damp cellar, injected damp-proofing, internal waterproofing where external walls are partially inaccessible, and repair of foundations built in contact with earth. The drawings also show drainage, external sealing, and breathable or hacked-off plaster options.
